name: Flexenpass
kurzbeschreibung: The 1,773 m high Flexenpass links Tyrol and Vorarlberg with historic rock galleries, steep gorges, and sweeping alpine vistas.
dauer: Driving time approx. 30 minutes; as an excursion with hiking 2 to 4 hours
preis: Free of charge and toll-free; parking at ski resorts partially subject to fees
oeffnungszeiten: Generally open year-round (subject to temporary closures in severe winter conditions or avalanche risk)
beschreibung:
Overview

The historic Flexenpass connects the Tyrolean Lechtal and the Arlberg region with the Vorarlberg Klostertal and the world-renowned winter sports resorts of Zürs and Lech am Arlberg at an elevation of 1,773 meters. Nestled between the towering rock massifs of the Lechquellen Mountains to the west and the Lechtal Alps to the east, the mountain pass has served for centuries as a vital transit link across the western Austrian high Alps. The route gained worldwide fame primarily through the daring historical Flexenstraße, blasted into sheer rock faces in the late 19th century and featuring listed avalanche galleries made of massive natural stone. Motorists, motorcyclists, and cyclists traverse an impressive masterpiece of late 19th-century road engineering, accompanied by breathtaking drops into the rugged Flexen and Hölltobel gorges and wide mountain panoramas.

Route & Requirements

The pass road branches off the Arlbergstraße B197 at Alpe Rauz near St. Christoph am Arlberg and ascends as the B198 over nearly six kilometers to the summit and onwards to Zürs. The road is fully paved, two-lane, and well maintained, with a maximum gradient of around ten percent, featuring several hairpin bends and arched avalanche galleries. The route is easily manageable for cars and experienced camper van drivers; caravans and oversize vehicles must observe local seasonal restrictions. Road cyclists consider the climb a classic challenge, though bright front and rear lights and reflective clothing are essential when passing through the galleries. Around the mountain saddle, scenic alpine hiking trails – such as the path to Zürsersee or crossings into the Karhorn massif – offer rewarding mountain treks. Sturdy hiking shoes are required away from the paved road.

Visit & Arrival

The Flexenpass road is generally open year-round, though temporary closures may occur during extreme winter snowstorms or elevated avalanche danger (winter tires and snow chain regulations apply). Drivers arrive from Tyrol via the A12 Inntal motorway and S16 Arlberg expressway to St. Anton am Arlberg, then continue over the Arlbergpass to Alpe Rauz. From Vorarlberg, access leads via Bludenz through the Klostertal. Regular ski buses and regional VVT and Landbus routes operate directly from St. Anton am Arlberg railway station across the Flexenpass to Zürs and Lech.

Tips

Pull over at designated scenic viewing bays just before the historic natural stone galleries to take photographs of the arched stonework and dramatic mountain chasms. In summer, combine your pass drive with a peaceful break at pristine Zürsersee or an afternoon coffee in Lech am Arlberg.
